trust_decision.summary: The static-API-key file decides which principal a presented key is; at the pinned commit it accepts duplicate entries in allowed_keys/users and resolves a key to the FIRST matching index, so a key written for one static user authenticates as another, and static-user privilege is not uniform (root/admin/viewer roles are granted by name in the RBAC model). The published fix (PR #11393, branch fix/11392-static-api-key-duplicates) adds a duplicate guard on that config-validation path.

landing_point.why: The summary only says 'improper authorization'; the first stop for API-key authorization is the static-key validator, where isTokenAllowed maps a token to the first matching configured index and getUser turns that index into a username.

fix_sites.entry_point: API-key authentication used by every REST and gRPC request (composer.New -> ApiKey.ValidateAndExtract; gRPC via adapters/handlers/grpc/v1/auth/auth.go:62)
fix_sites.module_kind: Go authentication usecase package (startup config validation of config.StaticAPIKey)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Every static principal is stamped IsGlobalOperator=true (usecases/auth/authentication/apikey/client.go:94-97), so a solver can argue all static users are equivalent operators and that two config entries resolving one key to another name is harmless config hygiene rather than an authorization flaw - ignoring that root/admin/viewer privileges are granted per username in usecases/auth/authorization/rbac/model.go:203-260.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The documented 'one user, multiple keys' form (all keys map to Users[0]) and the equal-length positional users/keys form are both legitimate and tested; a fix that requires users to be unique, or that forces users and keys to the same length, breaks them. An over-broad dedupe inside isTokenAllowed (returning an error whenever a key matched twice) would also break the deliberate single-user fallback in getUser.

O6_input_shapes: environment variables: AUTHENTICATION_APIKEY_USERS / AUTHENTICATION_APIKEY_ALLOWED_KEYS as comma-joined strings (usecases/config/environment.go:360-368)
single user + many keys (all keys resolve to Users[0])
missing/empty strings entries (already rejected by length checks)

O7_producer.where: usecases/config/environment.go:360-368 (env path, strings.Split with no trim or dedup) and usecases/config/config_handler.go:160 (YAML path); both feed wrapper.New -> NewStatic at usecases/auth/authentication/apikey/wrapper.go:30

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second comma-joined credential list (e.g. per-namespace static keys, or APIKEY_READONLY_KEYS) built with strings.Split and no trim/dedup
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This file already hand-rolls several list env vars this way (AUTHORIZATION_ADMINLIST_USERS at :375-377), so a maintainer adding another credential source would copy the same pattern and inherit the duplicate ambiguity.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A per-index role list paired to APIKey.Users (e.g. APIKEY_USERS_ROLES joined positionally), or grants computed by position instead of name
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The model already derives static-user privilege from the same APIKey.Users slice via slices.Contains at :208/:227/:245; extending it to per-position roles is the natural next step and would make duplicate/misaligned entries escalate privilege.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The static-key import path resolving user -> key by scanning Users and keeping the last match
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the only other consumer of AllowedKeys; a maintainer extending the experimental import endpoint could add another resolution rule here without reusing the auth package's first-match semantics.

O9_family: CWE-285 improper authorization (credential-to-principal misattribution from ambiguous duplicate static-key configuration)
